text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
- After corrections in platinum and palladium on Thursday, prices are poised to target fresh highs, analysts said.
Gold could tick higher, while silver was expected to consolidate before steaming to the upside, they added.
PLATINUM -
The market should have enough buying power to score fresh upside targets in the short term and possibly later on Friday.
"That is looking like a very nice upside break and I think it will carry through. There seems to be enough buying power there," said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst.
"It should clear $420 and maybe $430, but I think $440 is asking for a bit much," she added, referring to the July Nymex contract.
The high numbers would not be maintained, however, she said.
On Thursday, July platinum ended down 20 cents at $410.30 after hitting a fresh contract high at $420. The spot market ended in New York bid at $411.50, off a high of $425.
Analyst Peter Rehmer of Elliott Wave International agreed that prices should resume an upward tilt.
"Confidence is a little thin given the choppy pattern of the rebound from $406.50, but ideally platinum will rally at least slightly above the $418.0/$420.50 highs," he said.
At 0730 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $409.00/412.00, down $2.50 from Thursday's New York close.
PALLADIUM -
This market should also try the upside after the spot market ended weaker in New York at $193 from $201.
"This rebound should at least challenge the $205.00 high, and will ideally carry up further -- $214.20 remains a good upside objective," said Rehmer.
Gifford said Nymex June prices should target $210 and then $220, even though the market was overbought. June ended down $9.40 at $193.25 on Thursday.
But after attaining further upside targets, an "explosive sell-off" would follow, she warned.
At 0730 GMT spot palladium was quoted at $188.00/191.00, down $5.00 from Thursday's New York close.
GOLD -
Prices should tick higher, said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.

"Gold continues to maintain an upward bias with underlying support holding. The technical indicators are also pushing upwards, as we continue to favour further upside challenges," he said in a commentary.
Support should be seen at the convergence of the 10-day moving average at $343.21 and the 30-day average of $342.86. Initial resistance was seen at $346.
At 0730 GMT spot gold was quoted at $345.30/345.80, down 20 cents from Thursday's New York close.
SILVER -
Consolidation was likely to be seen after the spot market bounced to the $4.80s.
Technical indicators were drifting sideways, with nearby resistance seen at Thursday's peak of $4.85 and support at $4.70.
At 0730 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.83/4.85, unchanged from Thursday's New York close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
